title: Backfill TTFS/TTFP for existing tenants into analytics datasets
author: Mei Lin
release_notes: Internal only. Adds a one-time (and rerunnable) backfill job to populate onboarding TTFS/TTFP metrics for pre-checklist tenants to support pre/post comparisons on KPI dashboards.
description:
Context: As part of guided onboarding + first production launch checklist, we need baseline TTFS (time-to-first-success) and TTFP (time-to-first-production-traffic) for tenants that existed before onboarding event emission was deployed. This PR adds a batch backfill job that derives TTFS/TTFP from existing gateway request logs + usage/metering tables, writes results into the analytics dataset consumed by the onboarding KPI dashboards, and includes guardrails for idempotency and data quality.

What this does: (1) Introduces a scheduled/runnable batch job `onboarding_metrics_backfill` that computes TTFS and TTFP per tenant. (2) Implements SQL-based derivation using: first successful 2xx inference request timestamp for TTFS; first production-eligible traffic timestamp for TTFP (definition aligned with PM-751; see details below). (3) Writes results into `analytics.onboarding_ttfs_ttfp_backfill_v1` and upserts into the canonical `analytics.onboarding_tenant_metrics_v1`. (4) Adds basic data quality checks + freshness monitoring hooks (row count deltas, null rate ceilings, clock skew sanity checks). (5) Adds a dry-run mode for validation and a sampling tool to compare backfilled values against a small set of manually verified tenants.

Metric definition notes (aligned to PM-751): TTFS = time between `tenant_created_at` and first successful inference response (HTTP 2xx) for the Hosted API, excluding Console-only traffic and excluding synthetic health checks. TTFP = time between `tenant_created_at` and first production-eligible inference traffic, defined as the first 2xx request that matches any of: (a) request includes a non-default user agent (not quickstart templates) OR (b) request volume >= threshold across a rolling window (configurable; default 50 requests in 60 min) OR (c) request originates from a key labeled/flagged as production in control plane metadata. For backfill, we only have (a) and (b) reliably; (c) is best-effort based on historical key labels.

Why logs+usage: Event-based instrumentation (gateway emission) is the source of truth for new tenants, but older tenants require derivation from existing datasets. This job lets us compare pre/post launch and reduces bias in the onboarding funnel baselines.

Operational notes: The job is designed to be rerunnable and idempotent by (tenant_id, metric_version). We partition writes by `cohort_date` (tenant created date) and use merge/upsert semantics in the analytics warehouse. Runtime on prod-like staging data: ~18 minutes for 90-day window, ~1h10m for 12-month window at default warehouse size. Includes a `--window-start` / `--window-end` option to chunk backfills.

Privacy: No prompt text, no request bodies, and no end-user identifiers are pulled. Only tenant_id, timestamps, model_id, response status, token counts, and coarse user-agent category (enum) are used.

Rollout: This PR only adds the job + dataset wiring; execution will be coordinated with Telemetry (Logan/Nadia) after dashboards are ready and we have a validated dry-run in staging.

Test plan: Unit tests for metric derivation helpers; integration test against a local DuckDB fixture; staging dry-run validating row counts and sampling 20 known tenants; verify dashboards read from canonical table without breaking.
commits: add onboarding backfill job skeleton + CLI args
derive ttfs from gateway logs (first 2xx) with filters
add ttfp derivation using UA category + volume threshold heuristic
write to analytics tables with partitioning + idempotent upsert
data quality checks: null rate, negative durations, skew, row deltas
notable_snippets: TTFS derivation (pseudo): SELECT tenant_id, MIN(request_ts) AS first_success_ts FROM gateway_requests WHERE status_code BETWEEN 200 AND 299 AND endpoint IN ('/v1/chat/completions','/v1/completions','/v1/embeddings') AND is_console_traffic = FALSE AND is_healthcheck = FALSE GROUP BY tenant_id;
TTFP heuristic: first_success_ts where (ua_category IN ('custom','sdk_prod') OR requests_60m >= :threshold) ORDER BY request_ts ASC LIMIT 1;
review_conversation:
2025-03-08 Logan Wright: Can we guarantee idempotency if the job is rerun with a different window? Also, please document which table is canonical for dashboards.
2025-03-08 Mei Lin (author): Added (tenant_id, metric_version) merge key and ensured we only update when computed_ts is earlier; added a note in the runbook that dashboards should read `analytics.onboarding_tenant_metrics_v1` only.
2025-03-09 Nadia Rahman: UA classification looks brittle. Can we avoid raw UA strings and only store an enum? Also, ensure we’re not joining on high-cardinality fields.
2025-03-09 Mei Lin (author): Updated pipeline to categorize UA into enum buckets at read time; we persist only `ua_category`. Removed join on raw UA and switched to pre-aggregated request counts per tenant per hour.
2025-03-10 Chris Osei: Please align naming with PM-751 (ttfs_seconds, ttfp_seconds) and include a quick validation query for analysts.
2025-03-10 Mei Lin (author): Renamed output columns, updated schema comments, and added validation queries in the runbook (percentiles + null rate + negative duration checks).
2025-03-11 Caleb Johnson: Add a guardrail for clock skew / bad tenant_created_at values; we’ve seen a few tenants with migrated timestamps.
2025-03-11 Mei Lin (author): Added clamp + quarantine logic: if duration < 0 or > 365d, write to `analytics.onboarding_backfill_anomalies_v1` and exclude from canonical merge.
2025-03-12 Logan Wright: Approved after rerun. Please coordinate actual execution window with Telemetry; dashboards will assume a full 12-month backfill.
2025-03-12 Mei Lin (author): Ack; execution will be tracked in ENG-5844 and announced in #eng-platform once staged run is complete.
